subject: Private Offer - Northfield enterprise term & approval handoff
messages:
From: Tom Grant <tom.grant@northfield.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer request: Northfield enterprise licensing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. Procurement asked me to reach out formally to kick off a Private Offer in AWS Marketplace. High level: Northfield is evaluating a consolidated license for our ML platform teams, looking at committed usage across 24-36 months. Initial ask from procurement: can Redwood provide (1) pricing for a 36-month commitment and (2) a private-offer flow that allows our Procurement and Finance to approve the PO (they will need to see SOC2 + billing contact).

Key constraints from our side:
- We need an approval path that can be routed to our CFO for anything >$250k.
- We prefer a 36-month term but could consider 24 months if there are stronger pricing tiers.
- SOC2 report and a stub contract would help speed legal review.

Can you advise on the approval windows you support on AWS PO side and what approvals your team will need to finalize the pricing/term? Happy to get procurement included if we should align on specific language.

Cheers,
Tom Grant
VP, IT Infrastructure
Northfield Systems
procurement@northfield.com

[Attachment: Northfield_RFI.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Grant <tom.grant@northfield.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer request: Northfield enterprise licensing

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask and for the RFI. Looping in Vivek (sales) for pricing cadence and Marcus (finance) for approval/commit guidance. Quick answers up front:

- AWS private offers support buyer-side approval flows; typical approval window we see is 14–30 days but can be extended on request.
- For multi-year terms: 24 months is standard; 36 months is possible but may trigger additional legal review and executive approval on our end depending on discount depth.

Vivek / Marcus — can you review the attached RFI and propose a pricing/term recommendation (we should include an alternate 24-month with step-down pricing). Also confirm who internally must sign for a 36-month with ~30% list discount (approx).

Tom — I’ll attach our SOC2 summary and a draft PO/term sheet in the follow-up. If Procurement wants to be on the thread, add them and we’ll push a DocuSign draft and the AWS PO workflow.

Best,
Sooj
Soojín Lee | Senior Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Tom Grant <tom.grant@northfield.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer request: Northfield enterprise licensing

Tom / Soojin — thanks. Quick recommendation based on deal size signal in the RFI:

Proposal (we should present two options):
1) 24-month term — 28% off list; monthly billing via AWS Marketplace private offer; standard seller-managed activation; approval route: buyer PO -> Procurement -> CFO (if >$250k) within a 21-day window. This option minimizes legal exposure and keeps activation fast (3–5 business days after buyer approval).

2) 36-month term — 34% off list + 1% annual price escalate clause; requires internal Sales Director + Finance sign-off at Redwood (executive approval) due to longer exposure; recommend we pre-clear with Legal for any termination language. Activation via AWS PO but expect an additional 5–10 business days for our internal sign-off.

Evidence: we can provide SOC2 summary and our billing owner (billing@redwood.com). I’ve attached a pricing matrix and a DocuSign draft link below — Marcus, please flag any finance gating (proration rules, refund terms).

Next steps:
- Tom: confirm which option (1 or 2) Northfield prefers to move to a DocuSign + AWS PO draft.
- Soojin: I’ll prepare a pricing proposal and run the exec approval for 36m if they pick that.

Vivek
VP, Asia/AMER Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

[Attachment: pricing_proposal_northfield.xlsx]
Related link: https://docusign.example/sign/NORTH-2027-0530-draft

From: Tom Grant <tom.grant@northfield.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northfield.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer request: Northfield enterprise licensing

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear options. Procurement ran a quick read with Finance overnight. High-level reply from our CFO: we prefer 36 months to lock pricing, but only if there is a clear cap on annual increases and an exit clause tied to material service regressions. If Redwood needs extra time for internal approvals on the 36-month option, we can accept 30 days for the approval window but would like SOC2 + a copy of the draft contract to circulate to our legal team today.

Action items for Redwood:
- Send SOC2 (redacted ok) and the draft PO/contract (DocuSign link is fine)
- Confirm who signs on Redwood side for 36-month exec approval and expected timeline
- Confirm AWS PO approval window of 30 days (we can commit to that if needed)

Tom Grant
VP, IT Infrastructure
Northfield Systems
procurement@northfield.com

Tom — great, thanks. We can support the 36-month term with the constraints you noted, with the following clarifications: 

1) Approvals & signatories:
- Redwood will require Sales Director + VP Finance sign-off for any >30% list discount on multi-year deals; for this draft I will run exec approval with Marcus and expect a decision in 3 business days once pricing is finalized.
- For contract signing, Redwood will execute via DocuSign; for 36-month deals an executive-level signature (Sales Director) is standard on our side.

2) AWS PO flow & timeline:
- We can set a 30-day buyer approval window on the AWS private offer. Once buyer approves in AWS, activation typically happens within 3–7 business days after Redwood confirms internal sign-off.

3) Service & exit language:
- We will include a capped annual price escalator (<=1% per year) and an SLA-backed remediation clause limited to material regressions that materially impact availability/performance. Lauren (cc’d) — can you confirm standard legal language or flag anything Northfield should review?

Attachments I’m sharing now (redacted copies):
- SOC2_Northfield_stub.pdf (SOC2 summary)
- pricing_proposal_northfield.xlsx (detailed tiers for 24m vs 36m)
- docusign_northfield_draft.url (DocuSign draft landing page)

Related info: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/NORTH-2027-0530. Deal owner: Vivek Kulkarni.

Tom — if Procurement is ok, we’ll push the DocuSign draft and the AWS private offer simultaneously so you can route internally. Lauren — please scan the draft for any non-standard termination language; any redlines we’ll reconcile before we send the AWS PO.

Best,
